name: Grace Ives
label: True Panther Sounds
lede: Grace Ives wrote her first songs on a used Roland in a dorm at SUNY Purchase. Since then: three albums, one pink dye job, and a Pitchfork 8.4 for the record she made sober.

eras.title: A groovebox in a dorm room
eras.text: Grace Ives grew up in Gowanus, Brooklyn, studied graphic design, then started writing songs alone at SUNY Purchase on a used Roland. Her first release was five tracks on Bandcamp with a cover she made herself.

years.h: A School of Rock kid from Gowanus ends up at Purchase
years.p: Grace Ives played classic rock covers in School of Rock, started at the Maryland Institute College of Art, then moved to SUNY Purchase.
years.xp:
Ives's father is a cinematographer and her mother a former creative director in the music business. The Fader, in 2019, listed Avril Lavigne, Nelly Furtado, Madonna and New Order among her early loves.

The pop instincts came first. The bedroom synths came later, and only after she left art school.

years.h: She watches Mitski at a house show, then buys M.I.A.'s groovebox
years.p: At Purchase, Ives saw [[Mitski|fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5]] play a house show. She then bought a Roland MC-505 after reading that [[M.I.A.|7cf0ea9d-86b9-4dad-ba9e-2355a64899ea]] used one.
years.xp: The Fader reports she wrote her first songs alone in her dorm room and called them "cabin fever songs." The MC-505 stayed her main instrument for years: in 2026 she told PAN M 360 she had worked almost exclusively on a 505 until Girlfriend.

years.h: Really Hot goes up on Bandcamp with a cover Ives made herself
years.p: Five tracks, from "Me me me <3" to "Babyyy," released October 6, 2016.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it her debut EP. It was the whole catalog until a label found her.

eras.title: The first album
eras.text: Dots Per Inch, a New York label, put out her first album. Stereogum named her one of the year's best new bands.

years.src: Bandcamp: 2nd · The Fader · Flood · Stereogum: Best New Bands of 2019 · Interview
years.h: 2nd turns the dorm-room songs into a Dots Per Inch release
years.p: Out April 22, 2019, with [[Dots Per Inch|05f087cd-2259-498b-a57e-a888681c32c9]] label manager Tom Moore recording her in proper studio sessions while the MC-505 stayed in charge.
years.xp:
Vulture heard "Suicide's brittle-sounding dead-eyed stare, John Maus's wavering synth emissions" and K Records-style indie pop. Pitchfork noted she "never entertains boredom."

Stereogum put her on its Best New Bands of 2019 list. Flood says she worked the coat check at Baby's All Right, and Interview reports she also walked dogs by Razor scooter between East Williamsburg and Bushwick.

eras.title: Janky Star
eras.text: A three-album deal, a co-producer she first met on FaceTime, and a Best New Music tag from Pitchfork. Then a tour that ended somewhere darker.

years.big: a fire sign male who is 3000 miles away from you
years.h: Justin Raisen co-produces Janky Star, mostly over FaceTime
years.p: A psychic told Ives who her co-producer would be, she said in Nylon. Wary of co-producers, she worked with [[Justin Raisen|88728e3a-1dd6-4db4-a21f-d67d8d3dd5c0]] remotely during quarantine before they met in person.
years.xp:
Raisen has produced [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]] and Angel Olsen, per Nylon, and [[Sky Ferreira|05f3353e-e2d9-4344-a3c9-8009dd8e0427]], per Flood. Ives asked the psychic about the arrangement and was told: "There's a fire sign male who is 3000 miles away from you who's going to take this project to the next level."

She believes that was Raisen. Both are Aries, she said.

years.cap: Ives at Elsewhere Zone One, Brooklyn, September 2022
q: One of the best little pop albums of the year.
years.h: Janky Star arrives on True Panther, and Pitchfork tags it Best New Music
years.p: Out June 10, 2022 on True Panther Sounds and Harvest Records.
years.xp:
Flood says the songs deal with near-death experiences and drug dependency, with vocals shaped by Enya, Kate Nash and [[Kate Bush|4b585938-f271-45e2-b19a-91c634b5e396]]. "Shelly" is about a bartender who looked like the Twin Peaks character.

She told Flood she signed a three-album contract, and that it shaped how she wrote.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grace Ives · The Needle Drop
years.h: "Lullaby" on Kimmel, then a tour opening for Lykke Li
years.p: Ives played "Lullaby" on Jimmy Kimmel Live! in August 2022, and supported [[Lykke Li|cc7d4686-ea02-45fd-956e-94c1a322558c]]'s North American tour for Eyeye that year.
years.xp: She told Needle Drop her previous tour was just her, a tour manager and an Ableton session.

eras.title: Rock bottom, then Los Angeles
eras.text: After the tour came a three-year gap in releases. Ives got sober, moved west, and spent about two and a half years making the record she had not been able to make before.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit · Exclaim! · Atwood Magazine · Wikipedia: Girlfriend
years.h: Home from tour, she stops drinking and heads west
years.p: Ives says she stopped drinking in mid-2023 after the tour ended, then moved to Los Angeles to work with [[Ariel Rechtshaid|53ba7b2d-06c4-432a-81cc-ca7525adfec1]] and John DeBold.
years.xp:
Ives told The Line of Best Fit she came off the Janky Star tour with "a loose grasp on my own purpose," unfocused voice memos and heavy drinking. Her statement on the album later used the phrase "drinking, lying, and hiding."

She told Exclaim she went to her first sober concert with her father, learned to drive, and dyed her hair pink, a nod to her 15-year-old self. Heavy Duty Studios in Los Angeles, per Line of Best Fit, was one of the rooms. Wikipedia dates the recording to 2023 through 2025.

years.src: Stereogum: Grace Ives announces · Paste · Wikipedia: Girlfriend
years.h: Three singles drop the same day
years.p: "Avalanche," "Dance with Me" and "My Mans" are her first new music in three years, all made with Rechtshaid and DeBold.
years.xp:
Paste reports "Avalanche" began life as a ringtone. Ives was hesitant about "My Mans" until Rechtshaid compared it to Beyoncé's "Halo."

Stereogum and Wikipedia's album page date the drop to November 7. Wikipedia's artist page says October.

eras.title: Girlfriend
eras.text: The third album arrived with a Pitchfork 8.4, a first real band, and support slots with Robyn and Olivia Rodrigo.

q: The happiest song I've ever written.
years.src: Stereogum: Grace Ives announces · The Line of Best Fit
years.p: Stereogum called it a bleary synthpop jam about putting yourself back together after a breakup.

yt: Sound Check at Cherry Lane Theatre
years.h: Pitchfork gives Girlfriend an 8.4 and Best New Music
years.p: Hattie Lindert's review called it a "razor-sharp, refreshingly self-serious album." It's out on True Panther and Capitol.
years.xp:
Eleven songs in 36:36, written by Ives with Rechtshaid and DeBold, mixed by Dave Fridmann in Buffalo and mastered by Emily Lazar. Ives plays synths, piano, Mellotron and toy piano herself.

Wikipedia lists Metacritic at 86, Clash 8/10 and five stars each from The Guardian and The Independent. Paste dates it April 1; Wikipedia, Exclaim and Dork give March 20.

years.big: I let myself be embarrassed and let myself be cringe.
years.p: Ives told Paste, in a piece reviewing Girlfriend, that she stopped editing her worst moments out.
years.xp: Paste's reviewer said the record faces up to her past mistakes "half-wincing and half-winking."

years.src: Exclaim! · The Needle Drop · Stereogum: Grace Ives announces
yt: "Trouble" live at Rough Trade, NYC, May 26
years.h: Her first tour with a band runs from Philadelphia to London
years.p: The Girlfriend tour started April 17 in Philadelphia and ended June 16 at Village Underground in London.
years.xp: Ives told Exclaim she was rehearsing in Los Angeles with a full band for the first time. Needle Drop says a two-person band; she has said her earlier tours were solo.

years.h: Robyn takes her into Scotiabank Arena
years.p: Ives played Toronto's Scotiabank Arena on Robyn's Sexistential tour in September 2026.

years.h: Olivia Rodrigo's European leg comes next
years.p: She is booked to support [[Olivia Rodrigo|6925db17-f35e-42f3-a4eb-84ee6bf5d4b0]] on the European dates of the Unraveled Tour.
